title: The Queen of Versailles on Broadway #queenofversaillesmusical #kristi...
transcript: The Queen of Versailles on Broadway tells a cautionary tale, and I'm afraid it also might be one. Based on a 2012 documentary, we see Jackie Siegel climb her way from humble beginnings to celebrity and billionaire status, seemingly from a combination of ambition, strategy, luck, and delusion. The show begins with Jackie explaining to the cameras and the audience that she and her husband David are building themselves a replica of the Palace of Versailles to be the biggest home in America, quote, “because we can.” The rest of Act 1 meanders through a play-by-play of Jackie's life, void of any real drama — I was pretty bored. I thought Act 2 was a bit stronger since it got closer to what I believe is the point of the story, but it was nevertheless a slog and the whole thing felt pretty misguided. The score is forgettable but not offensive, as is the overall writing and direction. The performances are solid, with Nina White as the standout, portraying Jackie's daughter Victoria. Kristin Chenoweth's performance is good, albeit predictable — it definitely makes me wonder what she could have done in a meatier show. Really, my biggest issue here is that the “why” is muddy at best. Most of these characters are not very redeemable, and I spent Act 1 wondering why I should care — the tone is uneven, so I found it unclear if we were supposed to root for them or not. That question remains for me, but at least by the end of the show I came to some conclusions. I think the show is trying to say that if you spend your whole life wanting more, your life will pass you by. It would take a lot of work to showcase this message properly, and even in that case, I'd still wonder why these are the people whose story we need to tell in order to deliver it. In reference to the building of their palace, Victoria says something along the lines of “just because we can doesn't mean we should” — words of wisdom that I'd argue apply to this musical as well. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
